records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ בִּשְׁתֵּ֣י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה בִּשְׁנֵי־עָשָׂ֥ר חֹ֖דֶשׁ בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And it was in [the] twelfth year, in [the] twelfth month, on [the] first of the month, came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: In the twelfth month of the twelfth year, on its first day, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.1: And it came about in the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, on the first of the month, [that] the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

R.1: On the first day of the twelfth month, in the twelfth year of our exile, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

decisions.choice: the twelfth year, the twelfth month, the first day: March 585 BC
decisions.reason: Counted from Jehoiachin's exile, the date falls in March 585 BC (stated from general knowledge), two months after the news of Jerusalem's fall reached the exiles (33:21).

decisions.choice: the last two oracles against Egypt
decisions.reason: Verses 2-16 are a lament over Pharaoh, set in lines as poetry. Verses 17-32 are a dirge that sends Egypt down to the world of the dead, where it joins the nations that fell before it; they are set as prose.

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me, saying (L); came to me (B); The LORD gave me this message (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. Readable puts the day first and says what the years are counted from, as in 20:1.

records.heading: A lament for Pharaoh

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם שָׂ֤א קִינָה֙ עַל־פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֔יִם וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֔יו כְּפִ֥יר גּוֹיִ֖ם נִדְמֵ֑יתָ וְאַתָּה֙ כַּתַּנִּ֣ים בַּיַּמִּ֔ים וַתָּ֣גַח בְּנַהֲרוֹתֶ֗יךָ וַתִּדְלַח־מַ֨יִם֙ בְּרַגְלֶ֔יךָ וַתִּרְפֹּ֖ס נַהֲרוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: Son of man, take up a lament over Pharaoh king of Egypt, and say to him: A young lion of [the] nations you were likened, but you [are] like the monster in the seas; and you burst forth in your rivers, and you muddied [the] waters with your feet, and you fouled their rivers.
pieces: Son of man, raise a lament over Pharaoh king of Egypt \q and say to him, \q You think of yourself as a lion among the nations, \q but you are like a monster in the seas, \q thrashing about in your rivers, churning the water with your feet \q and muddying the streams.

L.2: Son of man, take up a lament over Pharaoh king of Egypt, \q and say to him, \q A young lion of the nations you thought yourself, \q but you [are] like the monster in the seas; \q you burst out in your rivers and stirred up the waters with your feet, \q and fouled their rivers.

R.2: Son of man, sing a funeral song about Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. \q Say to him, \q You think you are like a young lion among the nations, \q but you are really like a monster in the water. \q You splash around in your rivers and stir up the water with your feet. \q You make the rivers muddy.

decisions.choice: son of man: a mortal, as God addresses Ezekiel
decisions.reason: See the note at 2:1.

decisions.choice: a lament over Pharaoh
decisions.reason: See the note at 19:1. Verses 2-16 are a lament, sung over Pharaoh before his fall; verse 16 calls it so. They are set in lines as poetry.

decisions.choice: a young lion of the nations you thought yourself
alternatives: you are destroyed, young lion of the nations
decisions.reason: The verb may mean "you were likened", "you likened yourself" or, from a word spelled the same, "you are destroyed". Pharaoh sees himself as a lion, the king of beasts; the LORD sees a river monster.

decisions.choice: the monster in the seas: the river monster of 29:3
decisions.reason: See 29:3. "The seas" here are the great waters of the Nile (Isaiah 19:5).

decisions.choice: stirring and fouling the waters: troubling the nations
decisions.reason: The monster churns the river into mud. Pharaoh disturbed the peace of the nations with his schemes.

decisions.choice: no quotation marks; funeral song (R)
decisions.reason: The lament is what Ezekiel is told to say, so it takes no quotation marks. Readable says "funeral song" for *qinah*, as in 19:1.

records.source: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וּפָרַשְׂתִּ֤י עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶת־רִשְׁתִּ֔י בִּקְהַ֖ל עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וְהֶעֱל֖וּךָ בְּחֶרְמִֽי׃
records.gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: And I will spread over you my net with a company of many peoples, and they will bring you up in my net.
pieces: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: \q I will throw {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} net over you \q with a throng of many peoples, \q and they will drag you up in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} net.

L.3: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: \q I will spread over you {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} net \q with an assembly of many peoples, \q and they will haul you up in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} net.

R.3: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: \q I will throw {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} net over you. \q Many nations will come together, \q and they will pull you out of the water in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} net.

decisions.choice: my net: the LORD hunts the monster
decisions.reason: The LORD catches the monster as a hunter or fisherman does, as he caught Zedekiah in his net (12:13; 17:20). The many peoples are his helpers.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula.

records.source: וּנְטַשְׁתִּ֣יךָ בָאָ֔רֶץ עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה אֲטִילֶ֑ךָ וְהִשְׁכַּנְתִּ֤י עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ כָּל־ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְהִשְׂבַּעְתִּ֥י מִמְּךָ֖ חַיַּ֥ת כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And I will abandon you on the land; on [the] face of the field I will hurl you; and I will make settle on you all [the] birds of the heavens, and I will satisfy with you [the] beasts of all the earth.
pieces: I will leave you on the land \q and fling you onto the open field. \q I will let all the birds of the sky settle on you \q and let the wild animals of the whole earth gorge themselves on you.

L.4: And I will leave you on the land; \q on the face of the field I will hurl you; \q and I will make all the birds of the heavens settle on you, \q and I will fill the beasts of all the earth with you.

R.4: I will throw you onto dry land. \q I will leave you lying in an open field. \q All the birds will land on you, \q and wild animals from all over the earth will eat you until they are full.

decisions.choice: the monster left on land: the words of 29:5
decisions.reason: A water monster on dry land dies and becomes food for birds and beasts, as 29:5 said.

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֥י אֶת־בְּשָׂרְךָ֖ עַל־הֶֽהָרִ֑ים וּמִלֵּאתִ֥י הַגֵּאָי֖וֹת רָמוּתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And I will put your flesh on the mountains, and I will fill the valleys [with] your height.
pieces: I will spread your flesh on the mountains \q and fill the valleys with your carcass.

L.5: And I will lay your flesh upon the mountains \q and fill the valleys [with] your height.

R.5: I will scatter your flesh on the mountains \q and fill the valleys with your dead body.

decisions.choice: your height: the huge heap of your carcass
decisions.reason: The word means height, and seems to describe the great mass of the monster's body. With a small change it would mean "your worms" or "your rotting flesh".

decisions.choice: your carcass (B); your dead body (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "your height" (m1).

records.source: וְהִשְׁקֵיתִ֨י אֶ֧רֶץ צָפָתְךָ֛ מִדָּמְךָ֖ אֶל־הֶֽהָרִ֑ים וַאֲפִקִ֖ים יִמָּלְא֥וּן מִמֶּֽךָּ׃
records.gloss: And I will make drink [the] land [with] your flowing, from your blood, to the mountains, and [the] ravines will be filled from you.
pieces: I will drench the land with your flowing blood all the way to the mountains, \q and the ravines will be full of you.

L.6: And I will make the land drink your outflow, from your blood, up to the mountains, \q and the ravines will be filled with you.

R.6: Your blood will flow over the land all the way up to the mountains, \q and the ravines will be filled with your body.

decisions.choice: your outflow: what flows out of the carcass
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It seems to mean the blood and fluids that pour from the body.

records.source: וְכִסֵּיתִ֤י בְכַבּֽוֹתְךָ֙ שָׁמַ֔יִם וְהִקְדַּרְתִּ֖י אֶת־כֹּֽכְבֵיהֶ֑ם שֶׁ֚מֶשׁ בֶּעָנָ֣ן אֲכַסֶּ֔נּוּ וְיָרֵ֖חַ לֹא־יָאִ֥יר אוֹרֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And I will cover, when you are extinguished, [the] heavens, and I will darken their stars; [the] sun with cloud I will cover it, and [the] moon will not give its light.
pieces: When I snuff you out, I will veil the heavens \q and make their stars go dark. \q I will wrap the sun in a cloud, \q and the moon will give no light.

L.7: And when I snuff you out I will cover the heavens \q and darken their stars; \q the sun I will cover with a cloud, \q and the moon will not give its light.

R.7: When I put out your light, I will cover the sky \q and make the stars dark. \q I will hide the sun behind a cloud, \q and the moon will not shine.

decisions.choice: the darkening of sun, moon and stars: the signs of the day of the LORD
decisions.reason: The prophets describe the LORD's day of judgment with the darkening of the sky (Isaiah 13:10; Joel 2:10; Amos 8:9). Jesus uses the same picture (Matthew 24:29), and Revelation 6:12-13 takes it up. For Egypt it also recalls the plague of darkness (Exodus 10:21-23).

decisions.choice: when I snuff you out: when I put an end to you
decisions.reason: Pharaoh is pictured as a light that goes out, and with him the lights of heaven go dark.

records.source: כָּל־מְא֤וֹרֵי אוֹר֙ בַּשָּׁמַ֔יִם אַקְדִּירֵ֖ם עָלֶ֑יךָ וְנָתַ֤תִּי חֹ֨שֶׁךְ֙ עַֽל־אַרְצְךָ֔ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: All [the] lights of light in [the] heavens I will darken over you, and I will put darkness on your land, declaration of [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: All the bright lights of the heavens \q I will turn dark above you, \q and I will bring darkness over your land, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.8: All the lights of light in the heavens \q I will make dark over you, \q and I will set darkness on your land, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.8: I will make all the lights in the sky \q go dark above you. \q I will bring darkness over your land, \q says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the lights in the heavens: the sun, moon and stars of creation
decisions.reason: The word for "lights" is the one used in Genesis 1:14-16. The LORD who made them can darken them.

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B); says the Lord GOD (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *ne'um Adonai YHWH* in Ezekiel.

records.source: וְהִ֨כְעַסְתִּ֔י לֵ֖ב עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים בַּהֲבִיאִ֤י שִׁבְרְךָ֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם עַל־אֲרָצ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יְדַעְתָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will trouble [the] heart of many peoples, when I bring your destruction among [the] nations, to lands which you have not known.
pieces: I will trouble \q the hearts of many peoples \q when I bring news of your destruction among the nations, \q to lands you have never known.

L.9: And I will trouble \q the heart of many peoples, \q when I bring your destruction among the nations, \q to lands that you have not known.

R.9: Many nations will be upset \q when I destroy you \q and the news spreads among the nations, \q even to lands you have never known.

decisions.choice: your destruction
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "your breaking". The Greek translation reads "your captives", which would mean Egyptians taken into exile among the nations (stated from general knowledge). The Hebrew is kept: the news of Egypt's ruin goes far and wide.

decisions.choice: news of your destruction (B); the news spreads (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how Egypt's destruction reaches far lands.

records.source: וַהֲשִׁמּוֹתִ֨י עָלֶ֜יךָ עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֗ים וּמַלְכֵיהֶם֙ יִשְׂעֲר֤וּ עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ שַׂ֔עַר בְּעוֹפְפִ֥י חַרְבִּ֖י עַל־פְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְחָרְד֤וּ לִרְגָעִים֙ אִ֣ישׁ לְנַפְשׁ֔וֹ בְּי֖וֹם מַפַּלְתֶּֽךָ׃ס
records.gloss: And I will make appalled over you many peoples, and their kings will shudder over you [with] shuddering, when I brandish my sword before their faces; and they will tremble every moment, each for his life, on [the] day of your downfall.
pieces: I will make many peoples appalled at you, and their kings will shudder with horror over you \q when I brandish {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword before them. \q They will tremble every moment, each one for his own life, \q on the day of your fall.

L.10: And I will make many peoples appalled over you, and their kings will shudder with horror over you, \q when I brandish {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword before their faces; \q and they will tremble every moment, each for his life, \q on the day of your downfall.

R.10: Many nations will be shocked at what happened to you. Their kings will shake with horror \q when I swing {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword in front of them. \q Every one of them will tremble all the time, afraid for his own life, \q on the day you fall.

decisions.choice: shudder with horror: the verb is doubled
decisions.reason: As in 27:35, the noun beside its verb adds force.

decisions.choice: each for his life: each king fears for himself
decisions.reason: The kings who see Pharaoh fall fear that they will be next.

records.source: כִּ֛י כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה חֶ֥רֶב מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל תְּבוֹאֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: For thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: [The] sword of [the] king of Babylon will come to you.
pieces: For the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: \q The sword of the king of Babylon will come against you.

L.11: For thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: \q The sword of the king of Babylon will come upon you.

R.11: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: \q The army of the king of Babylon will attack you.

decisions.choice: the sword of the king of Babylon: the picture explained
decisions.reason: The net and the sword of the LORD (verses 3, 10) are the army of Babylon (30:24-25).

decisions.choice: The army
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sword stands for.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula.

records.heading: The sword of Babylon

records.source: בְּחַרְב֤וֹת גִּבּוֹרִים֙ אַפִּ֣יל הֲמוֹנֶ֔ךָ עָרִיצֵ֥י גוֹיִ֖ם כֻּלָּ֑ם וְשָֽׁדְדוּ֙ אֶת־גְּא֣וֹן מִצְרַ֔יִם וְנִשְׁמַ֖ד כָּל־הֲמוֹנָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: By [the] swords of mighty men I will make fall your multitude, [the] ruthless of [the] nations all of them; and they will devastate [the] pride of Egypt, and will be destroyed all its multitude.
pieces: I will make your hordes fall by the swords of warriors, \q all of them the most ruthless of nations. \q They will shatter the pride of Egypt, \q and all its hordes will be destroyed.

L.12: By the swords of mighty men I will make your multitude fall, \q the ruthless of the nations, all of them; \q and they will devastate the pride of Egypt, \q and all its multitude will be destroyed.

R.12: I will let soldiers from the cruelest of all nations \q kill your crowds of people with their swords. \q They will crush Egypt's pride, \q and all its people will be destroyed.

decisions.choice: the ruthless of the nations: Babylon's army
your multitude: Egypt's hordes

records.source: וְהַֽאֲבַדְתִּי֙ אֶת־כָּל־בְּהֶמְתָּ֔הּ מֵעַ֖ל מַ֣יִם רַבִּ֑ים וְלֹ֨א תִדְלָחֵ֤ם רֶֽגֶל־אָדָם֙ ע֔וֹד וּפַרְס֥וֹת בְּהֵמָ֖ה לֹ֥א תִדְלָחֵֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will destroy all its cattle from beside many waters, and will not muddy them [the] foot of a human again, and [the] hooves of cattle will not muddy them.
pieces: I will destroy all its cattle \q beside the abundant waters. \q No human foot will churn them again, \q and no hooves of cattle will muddy them.

L.13: And I will destroy all its cattle \q from beside many waters; \q and the foot of a human will not muddy them again, \q nor will the hooves of cattle muddy them.

R.13: I will kill all the cattle \q that live beside the great waters. \q No people will stir up the water with their feet again, \q and no cattle will make it muddy with their hooves.

decisions.choice: no foot will muddy the waters again: the monster of verse 2 is gone
decisions.reason: The one who churned the waters into mud is dead, and no one is left to stir them.

records.source: אָ֚ז אַשְׁקִ֣יעַ מֵֽימֵיהֶ֔ם וְנַהֲרוֹתָ֖ם כַּשֶּׁ֣מֶן אוֹלִ֑יךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: Then I will make their waters settle, and their rivers like oil I will make flow, declaration of [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: Then I will let their waters settle \q and make their rivers flow smooth as oil, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.14: Then I will make their waters settle, \q and their rivers like oil I will make flow, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.14: Then I will make their waters clear \q and make their rivers flow smoothly like oil, \q says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: waters settled, rivers like oil: the stillness of a land without life
decisions.reason: With no one to stir them, the waters grow clear and slow. The picture is of an emptied land (verse 15), though some read it as the peace that follows judgment.

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B); says the Lord GOD (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *ne'um Adonai YHWH* in Ezekiel.

records.source: בְּתִתִּי֩ אֶת־אֶ֨רֶץ מִצְרַ֜יִם שְׁמָמָ֣ה וּנְשַׁמָּ֗ה אֶ֚רֶץ מִמְּלֹאָ֔הּ בְּהַכּוֹתִ֖י אֶת־כָּל־י֣וֹשְׁבֵי בָ֑הּ וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: When I make [the] land of Egypt a desolation, and is desolate [the] land of its fullness, when I strike down all [who] dwell in it, then they will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: When I make the land of Egypt desolate and strip the land of all that fills it, \q when I strike down everyone living in it, \q then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.15: When I make the land of Egypt a desolation, and the land is stripped of its fullness, \q when I strike down all who dwell in it, \q then they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.15: I will make the land of Egypt empty. I will take away everything in it. \q I will kill everyone who lives there. \q Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: its fullness: all that fills it
decisions.reason: The word means everything a land holds: its people, cattle and goods.

decisions.choice: then they will know that I am the LORD
decisions.reason: The refrain follows the settled wording (see 6:7); Literal and Balanced write "then" in lowercase because the refrain ends a sentence that begins with "when".

records.source: קִינָ֥ה הִיא֙ וְק֣וֹנְנ֔וּהָ בְּנ֥וֹת הַגּוֹיִ֖ם תְּקוֹנֵ֣נָּה אוֹתָ֑הּ עַל־מִצְרַ֤יִם וְעַל־כָּל־הֲמוֹנָהּ֙ תְּקוֹנֵ֣נָּה אוֹתָ֔הּ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ
records.gloss: A lament it [is], and they will chant it; [the] daughters of the nations will chant it; over Egypt and over all its multitude they will chant it, declaration of [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: This is a lament, and it will be chanted; \q the women of the nations will chant it. \q Over Egypt and all its hordes they will chant it, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.16: This [is] a lament, and they will chant it; \q the daughters of the nations will chant it; \q over Egypt and over all its multitude they will chant it, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.16: This is a funeral song. People will sing it. \q The women of the nations will sing it. \q They will sing it for Egypt and all its people, \q says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the daughters of the nations will chant it: the mourning women
decisions.reason: Women led the singing of laments (2 Samuel 1:24; Jeremiah 9:16-19). The women of the nations will mourn Egypt.

decisions.choice: the women of the nations (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "daughters"; Balanced and Readable say that grown women are meant.

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B); says the Lord GOD (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *ne'um Adonai YHWH* in Ezekiel.

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ בִּשְׁתֵּ֣י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And it was in [the] twelfth year, on [the] fifteenth of the month, came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: It was the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, when the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.17: And it came about in the twelfth year, on the fifteenth of the month, [that] the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

R.17: On the fifteenth day of a month in the twelfth year of our exile, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

decisions.choice: the twelfth year, the fifteenth of the month: probably March 585 BC; the month is not named
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives no month. If it is the month of verse 1, the oracle came two weeks later, in March 585 BC. The Greek translation reads "the first month", which would put it a year earlier, in April 586 BC (stated from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: Egypt's descent to the world of the dead
decisions.reason: The last oracle on Egypt (verses 17-32) pictures the underworld as a great burial place where each fallen nation lies with its dead: Assyria, Elam, Meshech and Tubal, Edom, the princes of the north and the Sidonians. Pharaoh joins them. Isaiah 14:9-20 has a similar picture of the king of Babylon.

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me, saying (L); came to me (B); The LORD gave me this message (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. Readable says what the years are counted from, as in 20:1.

records.heading: Egypt among the fallen

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם נְהֵ֛ה עַל־הֲמ֥וֹן מִצְרַ֖יִם וְהוֹרִדֵ֑הוּ א֠וֹתָהּ וּבְנ֨וֹת גּוֹיִ֧ם אַדִּרִ֛ם אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ תַּחְתִּיּ֖וֹת אֶת־י֥וֹרְדֵי בֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: Son of man, wail over [the] multitude of Egypt, and bring it down, it and [the] daughters of majestic nations, to [the] earth of [the] lowest parts, with [those who] go down [to the] pit.
pieces: Son of man, wail for the hordes of Egypt and send them down, Egypt and the daughters of mighty nations, to the world below, with those who go down to the pit.

L.18: Son of man, wail over the multitude of Egypt, and bring it down, it and the daughters of majestic nations, to the land of the depths, with those who go down to the pit.

R.18: Son of man, mourn for the crowds of Egypt. Send them down to the world below, with the people of other mighty nations, to join those who go down to the pit.

decisions.choice: son of man: a mortal, as God addresses Ezekiel
decisions.reason: See the note at 2:1.

decisions.choice: bring it down: the prophet's word does what it says
decisions.reason: Ezekiel is told to bring Egypt down by his lament. The LORD's word through his prophet carries out what it announces (43:3; Jeremiah 1:10).

decisions.choice: the daughters of majestic nations: the nations themselves, or their mourning women
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean the mighty nations themselves, as "Daughter Zion" means Zion, or the women of verse 16 who sing the lament.

decisions.choice: the land of the depths: the world of the dead
decisions.reason: See 26:20. "The pit" is the grave.

records.source: מִמִּ֖י נָעָ֑מְתָּ רְדָ֥ה וְהָשְׁכְּבָ֖ה אֶת־עֲרֵלִֽים׃
records.gloss: Than whom are you more lovely? Go down and be laid with [the] uncircumcised!
pieces: Are you lovelier than anyone else? Go down and be laid to rest with the uncircumcised!

L.19: Whom do you surpass in loveliness? Go down and be laid with the uncircumcised!

R.19: Egypt, do you think you are more beautiful than other nations? Go down to the world of the dead and lie there among the uncircumcised, who died in disgrace!

decisions.choice: whom do you surpass in loveliness?: a taunt
decisions.reason: Egypt's beauty and pride will not save it. The question echoes 31:2 and 31:18.

decisions.choice: the uncircumcised: the dishonored dead
decisions.reason: See 28:10 and 31:18. The phrase returns again and again in verses 19-32.

decisions.choice: to the world of the dead ... who died in disgrace
decisions.reason: Readable says where Egypt goes down to and what lying with the uncircumcised means.

records.source: בְּת֥וֹךְ חַלְלֵי־חֶ֖רֶב יִפֹּ֑לוּ חֶ֣רֶב נִתָּ֔נָה מָשְׁכ֥וּ אוֹתָ֖הּ וְכָל־הֲמוֹנֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: In [the] midst of [the] slain of [the] sword they will fall; [the] sword is given; they have dragged her and all her multitudes.
pieces: They will fall among those killed by the sword. The sword is ready; Egypt is dragged away with all her hordes.

L.20: In the midst of the slain of the sword they will fall; the sword is appointed; they have dragged her off, and all her multitudes.

R.20: The Egyptians will die among those killed in war. The sword is ready to kill them. Egypt and all its crowds of people will be dragged away.

decisions.choice: the sword is appointed; they have dragged her off: a hard line
alternatives: drag her away with all her hordes!
decisions.reason: The words are brief and hard. "Dragged" may be a command ("drag her off!") or a past verb. Either way Egypt is hauled away to death.

records.source: יְדַבְּרוּ־ל֞וֹ אֵלֵ֧י גִבּוֹרִ֛ים מִתּ֥וֹךְ שְׁא֖וֹל אֶת־עֹֽזְרָ֑יו יָֽרְד֛וּ שָׁכְב֥וּ הָעֲרֵלִ֖ים חַלְלֵי־חָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: Will speak to him [the] chiefs of [the] mighty from [the] midst of Sheol with his helpers: They have come down, they lie, the uncircumcised, slain by [the] sword.
pieces: From the depths of Sheol the mightiest of warriors will speak to Pharaoh and his allies: "They have come down; they lie among the uncircumcised, killed by the sword."

L.21: The chiefs of the mighty will speak to him from the midst of Sheol, with his helpers: "They have come down; they lie [still], the uncircumcised, slain by the sword."

R.21: From deep in the grave the strongest leaders will speak to Pharaoh and his helpers. They will say, "They have come down here. They lie with the uncircumcised, who were killed in war."

decisions.choice: the dead speak to the newcomer
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah 14:9-10, the great dead greet the fallen king.

decisions.choice: the chiefs of the mighty: the great warriors and rulers of the past
decisions.reason: The first word means rams, the leaders of the flock, and so chiefs.

decisions.choice: with his helpers: Pharaoh's allies
decisions.reason: The words may mean that the chiefs speak to Pharaoh and his allies, or that they speak with Pharaoh's allies who went down before him.

decisions.choice: double quotation marks for the words of the dead
decisions.reason: Speech quoted inside the oracle takes double quotes.

decisions.choice: the grave (R); Sheol (L, B)
decisions.reason: Sheol follows the Isaiah table (see 31:15). "The pit" stays at every level.

records.source: שָׁ֤ם אַשּׁוּר֙ וְכָל־קְהָלָ֔הּ סְבִֽיבוֹתָ֖יו קִבְרֹתָ֑יו כֻּלָּ֣ם חֲלָלִ֔ים הַנֹּפְלִ֖ים בֶּחָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: There [is] Assyria and all her company; around him [are] his graves; all of them slain, fallen by the sword,
pieces: Assyria is there with all its company, its graves all around it, all of them slain, fallen by the sword.

L.22: There [is] Assyria and all her company; around it [are] its graves; all of them slain, fallen by the sword,

R.22: Assyria is there, with the graves of all its army around it. All of them were killed in war.

decisions.choice: Assyria: the empire that fell before Babylon
decisions.reason: Assyria ruled the Near East until Nineveh fell in 612 BC (31:3). It lies with its army in the world of the dead.

decisions.choice: around it are its graves: the king with his army buried around him
decisions.reason: The world of the dead is pictured as a burial ground, where each nation's ruler lies surrounded by the graves of his people.

decisions.choice: her ... his: the pronouns change
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses both feminine and masculine pronouns for Assyria, as nation and as king.

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִתְּנ֤וּ קִבְרֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ בְּיַרְכְּתֵי־ב֔וֹר וַיְהִ֣י קְהָלָ֔הּ סְבִיב֖וֹת קְבֻרָתָ֑הּ כֻּלָּ֤ם חֲלָלִים֙ נֹפְלִ֣ים בַּחֶ֔רֶב אֲשֶׁר־נָתְנ֥וּ חִתִּ֖ית בְּאֶ֥רֶץ חַיִּֽים׃
records.gloss: whose graves are set in [the] remotest parts of [the] pit, and her company is around her grave, all of them slain, fallen by [the] sword, who spread terror in [the] land of [the] living.
pieces: Their graves are set in the deepest parts of the pit, and its company lies around its grave. All of them were slain, fallen by the sword, who once filled the land of the living with terror.

L.23: whose graves are set in the remotest parts of the pit, and her assembly is round about her grave, all of them slain, those fallen by the sword, who spread terror in the land of the living.

R.23: Their graves are deep down in the pit. Its army lies all around its grave. All of them were killed in war, though they once made everyone afraid in the land of the living.

decisions.choice: the remotest parts of the pit: the deepest place of the dead
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of the king of Babylon in Isaiah 14:15.

decisions.choice: who spread terror in the land of the living: who were feared while they lived
decisions.reason: The land of the living is this world. The theme of the nations' terror, now ended, runs through verses 23-32.

records.source: שָׁ֤ם עֵילָם֙ וְכָל־הֲמוֹנָ֔הּ סְבִיב֖וֹת קְבֻרָתָ֑הּ כֻּלָּ֣ם חֲלָלִים֩ הַנֹּפְלִ֨ים בַּחֶ֜רֶב אֲֽשֶׁר־יָרְד֥וּ עֲרֵלִ֣ים׀אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ תַּחְתִּיּ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתְנ֤וּ חִתִּיתָם֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חַיִּ֔ים וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ כְלִמָּתָ֖ם אֶת־י֥וֹרְדֵי בֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: There [is] Elam and all her multitude around her grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sword, who went down uncircumcised to [the] earth of [the] lowest parts, who put their terror in [the] land of [the] living; and they bear their disgrace with [those who] go down [to the] pit.
pieces: Elam is there, with all its hordes around its grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sword. They went down uncircumcised to the world below, those who spread their terror in the land of the living. Now they bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.

L.24: There [is] Elam, and all her multitude, round her grave, all of them slain, those fallen by the sword, who went down uncircumcised to the land of the depths, who spread their terror in the land of the living; and they bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.

R.24: Elam is there, with all its people around its grave. All of them were killed in war. They went down in disgrace to the world below. Once they made everyone afraid in the land of the living. Now they bear their shame with those who go down to the pit.

decisions.choice: Elam: a kingdom east of Babylon
decisions.reason: Elam, with its capital at Susa, lay in what is now southwest Iran. It was crushed by Assyria in the seventh century BC (stated from general knowledge; compare Jeremiah 49:34-39).

decisions.choice: they bear their disgrace: their shame stays with them
decisions.reason: The proud nations that once caused terror now lie in shame.

records.source: בְּת֣וֹךְ חֲ֠לָלִים נָתְנ֨וּ מִשְׁכָּ֥ב לָהּ֙ בְּכָל־הֲמוֹנָ֔הּ סְבִֽיבוֹתָ֖יו קִבְרֹתֶ֑הָ כֻּלָּ֣ם עֲרֵלִ֣ים חַלְלֵי־חֶ֡רֶב כִּֽי־נִתַּ֨ן חִתִּיתָ֜ם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חַיִּ֗ים וַיִּשְׂא֤וּ כְלִמָּתָם֙ אֶת־י֣וֹרְדֵי ב֔וֹר בְּת֥וֹךְ חֲלָלִ֖ים נִתָּֽן׃
records.gloss: In [the] midst of [the] slain they have made a bed for her with all her multitude; around it [are] her graves; all of them uncircumcised, slain by [the] sword; for was put their terror in [the] land of [the] living, and they bear their disgrace with [those who] go down [to the] pit; in [the] midst of [the] slain it is put.
pieces: Among the slain a bed has been made for Elam with all its hordes, their graves around it, all of them uncircumcised, killed by the sword. Because their terror was spread in the land of the living, they now carry their disgrace with those who go down to the pit; they are laid among the slain.

L.25: In the midst of the slain they have made a bed for her with all her multitude, her graves around it; all of them uncircumcised, slain by the sword; because their terror was spread in the land of the living, and they bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit; in the midst of the slain it is placed.

R.25: A bed has been made for Elam among those killed in war, with the graves of all its people around it. All of them were uncircumcised and killed in war. They once made everyone afraid in the land of the living. Now they bear their shame with those who go down to the pit. They lie among those who were killed.

decisions.choice: a verse that largely repeats verse 24
decisions.reason: The verse goes over much of verse 24 again. The Greek translation lacks most of it (stated from general knowledge). The Hebrew is kept.

decisions.choice: a bed: a grave
decisions.reason: The grave is pictured as a bed where the dead lie (Isaiah 14:11; 57:2).

decisions.choice: Elam
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Elam, to whom "her" refers.

records.source: שָׁ֣ם מֶ֤שֶׁךְ תֻּבַל֙ וְכָל־הֲמוֹנָ֔הּ סְבִֽיבוֹתָ֖יו קִבְרוֹתֶ֑יהָ כֻּלָּ֤ם עֲרֵלִים֙ מְחֻ֣לְלֵי חֶ֔רֶב כִּֽי־נָתְנ֥וּ חִתִּיתָ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ חַיִּֽים׃
records.gloss: There [are] Meshech, Tubal and all her multitude; around him [are] his graves; all of them uncircumcised, pierced by [the] sword, for they put their terror in [the] land of [the] living.
pieces: Meshech and Tubal are there, with all their hordes, their graves around them, all of them uncircumcised, killed by the sword, because they once made the land of the living fear them.

L.26: There [are] Meshech, Tubal and all her multitude, its graves around it; all of them uncircumcised, pierced by the sword, for they spread their terror in the land of the living.

R.26: Meshech and Tubal are there, with the graves of all their people around them. All of them were uncircumcised and killed in war, because once they made everyone afraid in the land of the living.

decisions.choice: Meshech and Tubal: warlike peoples of Asia Minor
decisions.reason: See 27:13. They return as the people of Gog in 38:2-3 and 39:1.

records.source: וְלֹ֤א יִשְׁכְּבוּ֙ אֶת־גִּבּוֹרִ֔ים נֹפְלִ֖ים מֵעֲרֵלִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָרְדֽוּ־שְׁא֣וֹל בִּכְלֵֽי־מִלְחַמְתָּם֩ וַיִּתְּנ֨וּ אֶת־חַרְבוֹתָ֜ם תַּ֣חַת רָאשֵׁיהֶ֗ם וַתְּהִ֤י עֲוֺֽנֹתָם֙ עַל־עַצְמוֹתָ֔ם כִּֽי־חִתִּ֥ית גִּבּוֹרִ֖ים בְּאֶ֥רֶץ חַיִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And they do not lie with [the] mighty fallen of [the] uncircumcised, who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, and they put their swords under their heads, and their iniquities were on their bones, for [the] terror of [the] mighty [was] in [the] land of [the] living.
pieces: They do not lie with the fallen warriors of the uncircumcised, who went down to Sheol armed for war, their swords laid under their heads and their guilt resting on their bones, though the terror of these warriors was in the land of the living.

L.27: And they do not lie with the fallen mighty men of the uncircumcised, who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, and whose swords were put under their heads, and whose iniquities were on their bones; for the terror of the mighty men [was] in the land of the living.

R.27: They do not lie with the fallen heroes of the uncircumcised, who went down to the grave with their weapons. Their swords were placed under their heads, and their sins stayed on their bones. Those heroes once made everyone afraid in the land of the living.

decisions.choice: of the uncircumcised
alternatives: the fallen mighty men of old
decisions.reason: The Greek translation reads "of old" instead of "of the uncircumcised", which differs by little in Hebrew (stated from general knowledge). It would recall "the mighty men of old" of Genesis 6:4. The Hebrew is kept.

decisions.choice: weapons of war, swords under their heads: an honored warrior's burial
decisions.reason: Great warriors were buried with their weapons. Meshech and Tubal do not share that honor.

decisions.choice: their iniquities were on their bones
alternatives: their shields were on their bones
decisions.reason: The phrase is strange in a list of honors. Many think it once read "their shields were on their bones", which differs by a few letters in Hebrew. The standard text is kept.

decisions.choice: they do not lie: a statement, or a question
alternatives: Do they not lie with the fallen warriors?
decisions.reason: The words can also be read as a question: "Do they not lie with the fallen warriors?"

decisions.choice: the grave (R); Sheol (L, B)
decisions.reason: Sheol follows the Isaiah table (see 31:15). "The pit" stays at every level.

decisions.choice: iniquities (L); guilt (B); sins (R)
decisions.reason: *'Awon* follows the Isaiah table.

records.source: וְאַתָּ֗ה בְּת֧וֹךְ עֲרֵלִ֛ים תִּשָּׁבַ֥ר וְתִשְׁכַּ֖ב אֶת־חַלְלֵי־חָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: And you, in [the] midst of [the] uncircumcised you will be broken, and you will lie with [those] slain by [the] sword.
pieces: And you too, Pharaoh, will be broken among the uncircumcised and lie with those killed by the sword.

L.28: And you, in the midst of the uncircumcised you will be broken, and you will lie with those slain by the sword.

R.28: And you, Pharaoh, will be crushed and lie among the uncircumcised, with those killed in war.

decisions.choice: and you: Pharaoh
decisions.reason: The dirge turns to address Pharaoh directly, in the middle of the list of the dead.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one addressed.

records.source: שָׁ֣מָּה אֱד֗וֹם מְלָכֶ֨יהָ֙ וְכָל־נְשִׂיאֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁר־נִתְּנ֥וּ בִגְבוּרָתָ֖ם אֶת־חַלְלֵי־חָ֑רֶב הֵ֛מָּה אֶת־עֲרֵלִ֥ים יִשְׁכָּ֖בוּ וְאֶת־יֹ֥רְדֵי בֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: There [is] Edom, her kings and all her princes, who were put in their might with [the] slain of [the] sword; they with [the] uncircumcised lie, and with [those who] go down [to the] pit.
pieces: Edom is there, its kings and all its princes, who for all their might are laid with those killed by the sword. They lie with the uncircumcised, with those who go down to the pit.

L.29: There [is] Edom, her kings and all her princes, who for all their might are laid with those slain by the sword; with the uncircumcised they lie, and with those who go down to the pit.

R.29: Edom is there, with its kings and all its rulers. Even though they were powerful, they lie with those killed in war. They lie with the uncircumcised, with those who go down to the pit.

decisions.choice: Edom
decisions.reason: See 25:12 and chapter 35.

decisions.choice: princes (L, B); rulers (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *nasi'*.

records.source: שָׁ֣מָּה נְסִיכֵ֥י צָפ֛וֹן כֻּלָּ֖ם וְכָל־צִֽדֹנִ֑י אֲשֶׁר־יָרְד֣וּ אֶת־חֲלָלִ֗ים בְּחִתִּיתָ֤םמִגְבֽוּרָתָם֙ בּוֹשִׁ֔ים וַיִּשְׁכְּב֤וּ עֲרֵלִים֙ אֶת־חַלְלֵי־חֶ֔רֶב וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ כְלִמָּתָ֖ם אֶת־י֥וֹרְדֵי בֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: There [are the] chiefs of [the] north, all of them, and every Sidonian, who went down with [the] slain; in their terror, from their might, [they are] ashamed; and they lie uncircumcised with [the] slain of [the] sword, and they bear their disgrace with [those who] go down [to the] pit.
pieces: All the chiefs of the north are there, and all the Sidonians. They went down with the slain, put to shame for all the terror their might once caused. They lie uncircumcised with those killed by the sword and bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.

L.30: There [are] the chiefs of the north, all of them, and all the Sidonians, who went down with the slain; for all the terror of their might, they are ashamed; and they lie uncircumcised with the slain of the sword, and they bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.

R.30: All the leaders of the north are there, and all the people of Sidon. They went down in shame with those who were killed, even though their power once made people afraid. They lie with the uncircumcised, who were killed in war. They bear their shame with those who go down to the pit.

decisions.choice: the chiefs of the north and the Sidonians: the rulers of Syria and Phoenicia
decisions.reason: The "north" here is the region north of Israel, Syria and the Phoenician coast. Sidon was named in 28:20-23.

decisions.choice: chiefs: princes, rulers
decisions.reason: The word is not Ezekiel's usual word for "prince" (*nasi'*); it means a chief or ruler (Joshua 13:21; Micah 5:4).

records.source: אוֹתָם֙ יִרְאֶ֣ה פַרְעֹ֔ה וְנִחַ֖ם עַל־כָּל־הֲמוֹנ֑וֹ חַלְלֵי־חֶ֨רֶב֙ פַּרְעֹ֣ה וְכָל־חֵיל֔וֹ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: Them Pharaoh will see, and he will be comforted over all his multitude, slain by [the] sword, Pharaoh and all his army, declaration of [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over all his hordes, Pharaoh and all his army, killed by the sword, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.31: These Pharaoh will see, and he will be comforted over all his multitude, slain by the sword, Pharaoh and all his army, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.31: When Pharaoh sees them, he will be comforted about all his people who were killed. Pharaoh and all his army will be killed in war, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: he will be comforted: the grim comfort of a shared fate
decisions.reason: As the trees of Eden were comforted in 31:16, Pharaoh will find some consolation that other great nations lie there too.

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B); says the Lord GOD (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *ne'um Adonai YHWH* in Ezekiel.

records.source: כִּֽי־נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת־חִתִּיתִ֖י בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חַיִּ֑ים וְהֻשְׁכַּב֩ בְּת֨וֹךְ עֲרֵלִ֜ים אֶת־חַלְלֵי־חֶ֗רֶב פַּרְעֹה֙ וְכָל־הֲמוֹנֹ֔הנְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ
records.gloss: For I put my terror in [the] land of [the] living, and he will be laid in [the] midst of [the] uncircumcised with [the] slain of [the] sword, Pharaoh and all his multitude, declaration of [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: For I spread {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} terror in the land of the living. So Pharaoh and all his hordes will be laid among the uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.32: For I put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} terror in the land of the living; and he will be laid in the midst of the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword, Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.32: I spread terror of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the land of the living. But Pharaoh and all his people will lie among the uncircumcised, with those killed in war, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: I put my terror
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew reads "his terror"; the reading noted in the margin, followed here, is "my terror". With "his", the line would say that the LORD let Pharaoh spread terror in his lifetime; with "my", that the terror was the LORD's own, and he now ends Pharaoh's.

decisions.choice: the end of the oracles against Egypt
decisions.reason: The oracles on the nations end with Pharaoh among the dishonored dead. The next chapter returns to Ezekiel as watchman over Israel.

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B); says the Lord GOD (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *ne'um Adonai YHWH* in Ezekiel.
